_doc: THE CONTRACT for Sun & Steel sprites. Names, sizes and frame counts are binding. Raw AI images: games/tactics/art/raw/<name>.png (converted by tools/art/convert.py) or <name>_chibi.png (the chibi party's concepts); sprites: games/tactics/assets/sprites/sun_steel/<name>.<frame>.png (frame index from 0). A sprite with a "chain" is built by tools/art/rebuild.py from those exact tool steps (run from the repo root; rebuild.py adds --work) instead of convert.py. max_flicker caps how many pixels any frame may change against frame 0 beyond a 1 px bob, so idle frames can't flicker.

game.filter: nearest, 1 texel = 1 logical pixel (no mixed pixel densities)
game.board: 12 x 10 cells of 24 x 24 px (288 x 240), camera 3/4 top-down like a handheld tactics game
game.unit_anchor: unit sprites are 32 x 32; the unit stands centred on its 24 px cell with its feet on rows 28-30 of the canvas, so heads may overlap the cell above
game.light: single light from the top-left; 1 px dark outline (ink.0 or the darkest step of the local ramp; selective outlining allowed)
game.idle_animation: 4 frames at about 6 fps; the chibi party holds one pose and adds a 1 px bob on frames 1-2 plus a blink on a different frame per hero (the game starts each unit on a different frame); same silhouette centre and feet row
game.humanoid_height: each hero has its own target_height (px from the top of the head, mane or ears to the soles, before the 1 px outline): the chibi party is about 21-23 px, and tall ears or a mane raise a sprite's target on purpose, with the reason in its brief

sprites.name: unit_sun_knight
sprites.brief: Player hero, tank class: a lion cub knight in steel plate with gold trim, a crimson cape, a gold sun buckler and a short sword. The code mane pass grows a spiky sun-ray mane so it reads as a lion at 1x; --crown 2 lets the mane rise 2 px above the AI head (the first version's top was clipped flat), so target_height is 23, not 21. Faces right (3/4). Held on frame 0. Held key pose: every frame starts as one cleaned frame (touchup.py --lock with the whole canvas), so ear linings, fur flecks and robe folds that the AI drew differently in each pose don't flicker; eye_pass.py adds 2x3 eyes with a highlight, cheeks and the blink, and idle_bob.py adds the motion last (everything above the feet drops 1 px on frames 1-2). Blinks on frame 3.

sprites.name: unit_golem
sprites.brief: Enemy: a cute grumpy pebble golem of round chunky basalt stones with ember eyes, stubby arms and a moss tuft, darker than the heroes so it reads as the enemy at 1x. Faces the viewer, turned slightly left. Drawn in code by tools/art/draw_chibi.py from the concept in games/tactics/art/raw/unit_golem_chibi.png, because its pale or glowing design turned to speckle in crisp_convert.py; it matches the converted heroes (1 px ink outline, 2x3 eyes with a white highlight, rosy cheeks). Idle: 1 px squash, ember eyes flicker. max_flicker is 24, not 16: the squash and the flickering ember eyes are deliberate motion beyond a bob (13-20 pixels per frame).

sprites.name: unit_pyromancer
sprites.brief: Player hero, mage: a red panda cub in a crimson robe with gold trim, a ringed tail and a staff with an ember orb. Held on frame 1, the frame with the cleanest face; the recolour fixes violet strays from the palette snap and the patches give the muzzle a clean white edge. Faces right (3/4). Held key pose: every frame starts as one cleaned frame (touchup.py --lock with the whole canvas), so ear linings, fur flecks and robe folds that the AI drew differently in each pose don't flicker; eye_pass.py adds 2x3 eyes with a highlight, cheeks and the blink, and idle_bob.py adds the motion last (everything above the feet drops 1 px on frames 1-2). Blinks on frame 1.

sprites.name: unit_frost_blade
sprites.brief: Player hero, spellblade: a snow leopard cub swordfighter with pale blue-grey fur, a big clear white face, small round ears, dark rosettes, a big-cat muzzle and a thick ringed tail curling up behind, in bright blue armour with one steel shoulder plate and a short scarf, holding a pale cyan crystal sword. Faces right (3/4). Drawn in code by tools/art/draw_chibi.py from the concept in games/tactics/art/raw/unit_frost_blade_chibi.png, because its pale or glowing design turned to speckle in crisp_convert.py; it matches the converted heroes (1 px ink outline, 2x3 eyes with a white highlight, rosy cheeks). Idle: 1 px bob, blink on frame 3, a sword glint.

sprites.name: unit_ranger
sprites.brief: Player hero, ranger: a bunny archer with honey-tan fur, very tall ears through a forest-green hood and cloak, a gold sun clasp and a small bow. The tall ears are the bunny's silhouette, so target_height is 28 with the ears. Held on frame 0, the frame with the tidiest ears; five patches give the right ear the same two-pixel lining as the left. Faces right (3/4). Held key pose: every frame starts as one cleaned frame (touchup.py --lock with the whole canvas), so ear linings, fur flecks and robe folds that the AI drew differently in each pose don't flicker; eye_pass.py adds 2x3 eyes with a highlight, cheeks and the blink, and idle_bob.py adds the motion last (everything above the feet drops 1 px on frames 1-2). Blinks on frame 2.

sprites.name: unit_cleric
sprites.brief: Player hero, healer: a lamb with white wool as a few big smooth puffs, a large clear cream face, small floppy ears and curled gold horns, in a white robe with wide gold trim and a gold sun pendant, holding a short gold sceptre topped with a sun disc. Faces right (3/4). Drawn in code by tools/art/draw_chibi.py from the concept in games/tactics/art/raw/unit_cleric_chibi.png, because its pale or glowing design turned to speckle in crisp_convert.py; it matches the converted heroes (1 px ink outline, 2x3 eyes with a white highlight, rosy cheeks). Idle: 1 px bob, blink on frame 1, the sun disc twinkles.

sprites.name: tile_floor
sprites.brief: Shrine floor: weathered flagstones (stone ramp), low contrast and low saturation so units pop. Must tile seamlessly with itself in any grid (edges wrap). Structured detail (seams, chips, a few cracks), no random speckle.

sprites.name: tile_lava
sprites.brief: Hazard: molten lava (ember + gold ramps) with darker crust plates that drift between frames. Must tile seamlessly with itself on every frame. Brighter than the floor so the hazard is unmistakable.

sprites.name: prop_cover_rock
sprites.brief: Cover: a waist-high boulder (stone ramp) with a little moss (forest ramp), transparent background, placed on top of tile_floor. Short shadow toward the bottom-right drawn with opaque dark pixels (ordered dither allowed). Fills roughly the lower two-thirds of the cell.
